subject: AIC ranking and GOF results in NB pcount models

messages.author: b4d2eae4afc10686
messages.subject: AIC ranking and GOF results in NB pcount models
parts:
Hi all,

I am analyzing four years of population count data in the stacked format using pcount, with a relatively small data set (~18 sites across four years). I am comparing seven models containing different covariates to explain patterns of abundance using AIC. Initially, the models were run with a Poisson distribution, but c-hat values were high (3-9) and Nmixgof.test showed poor fits for many of the individual models (because of limited data set, we couldn’t do GOF on a global model). The models were re-run using the negative binomial mixture, which reduced c-hat (< 3), the parameter estimates seem stable with increasing K, and baseline detection probability decently high (~0.5). So, seems like the NB worked better for us. When we re-ranked models using AIC, we ended up with several competing models (delta AIC < 2) at the top. However, some of these top models still had failed GOF of fit tests (p < 0.05).

Assuming we shouldn't just ditch the analysis altogether because of failed GOF tests, my question then is whether we can use GOF as an additional criterion of support for distinguishing between top models. For example, if the top two models are < 1 different in AIC, but one GOF test fails and the other doesn’t, can we use that as evidence alongside AIC in determining which one may be a better fitting model? Given what I’ve read in this group on the fact that a failed GOF test could indicate structural problems in a model beyond overdispersion, I thought it could maybe be used in this context to find support for the best best model.

Two additional follow-ups:

1. Given we still potentially have some overdispersion based on our c-hat values, is there a further correction for negative binomial parameter estimates that needs to be applied, similar to what is done in summaryOD for Poisson models?

2. Is there any information in the Kery and Royle books or elsewhere on how to interpret/use the dispersion estimate in NB models? For instance, the alpha estimate was -1.02 and significant (p = 0.01), but I wasn't sure exactly what this means.

Any advice or useful literature suggestions would be greatly appreciated.
